note: ROADSTER: The Flying Car (https://roadster-the-flying-car-gamev28.vercel.app/) is capture-class: a single-file three.js game served by Vercel at the origin root. §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — no public upstream source repo exists (the captured text carries no github/gitlab/bitbucket reference for the project itself; the only repository credits are third-party library banners inside the bundled three.js source — mrdoob/three.js, toji/gl-matrix, mapbox/earcut, paper.js, GeometricTools, lightgl.js — and a GitHub search for the project finds nothing), so the mirror stands. Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, single pass verified idempotent — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → the entry document's inline <script type="module"> becomes readable/index-inline-1.pretty.js and the service-worker registration script becomes readable/index-inline-2.pretty.js (both pretties provably NOT byte-identical to their capture blocks; readable/index-inline-map.json records each block's exact byte range + sha256), the two inline <style> blocks become readable/index-inline-1|2.pretty.css, and the captured sw.js becomes readable/sw.pretty.js. The big script is a single-file bundle behind a tiny `__defs`/`__req` module registry: its first two statements (the registry object and the `__req` loader) are wholeFile build machinery, the next twelve statements are the vendor `__defs['<id>'] = function () { … };` module definitions (three.js r187dev three.core/three.module plus the ten examples/jsm postprocessing+shader addons) claimed wholeFile under the vendor rule (indexed, never sliced; the id set and content anchors are asserted), and everything from the app's `const THREE = __req('three.module.js');` on is the game's own app code — statement-aligned slices src/index-inline-1-NN.js at top-level statement boundaries (~250-350 line windows; oversized single declarations stay whole) with an exact 2-line provenance header. Every slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range. Stylesheet rule — the two inline <style> blocks are wholeFile sections, never sliced. Non-code payloads (icon-192.png, icon-512.png, og.jpg and the manifest.webmanifest data file) are hashed notRendered records (bytes + sha256, no pretty pass). The off-origin loads (the Google Fonts stylesheet + font origins, the gstatic firebase base the optional cloud-login path dynamic-imports) were never captured (socker precedent, PLAN §1) and have no derived layer; tools/capture.mjs --check lists them as external references. The bundle's module boundaries were decided from bytes (tools/probe-structure.mjs): the `__defs` registry IS a factory family (12 module factories), but every factory is a VENDOR module, so the whole region is wholeFile by the vendor rule (the turbopack README's "the vendor chunk stays wholeFile" gotcha adapted); there are 0 app factories, so the app code is a flat module and statement-aligned slices are its real shape. Identifiers in src/ carry the semantic rename campaign (PLAN §5): the script is AUTHORED, not minified, so tools/names.json renames only the genuinely opaque short bindings (single-letter globals, two/three-letter codes, the `_`-prefixed scratch family) and leaves the author's own semantic names alone; tools/apply-names.mjs applies them, tools/recover-scoped-map.mjs recovers rename-map.json, and this tool re-applies the map on every re-cut. The vendor `__defs`/`__req` loader and the twelve three.js module factories are never candidates. Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate.
